items.title: End of Mercenary Programmers
items.summary: Who are Mercenary programmers? Mercenary programmers are individuals with highly specialized technical skills, who can zip through the corporate bureaucracy, go past the red tape,…
items.content_html:
Who are Mercenary programmers?

Mercenary programmers are individuals with highly specialized technical skills, who can zip through the corporate bureaucracy, go past the red tape, work solo and in isolation with little or no guidance from the existing team and then deliver outcome really really fast. They work without burdening the existing team which feels magical. Their impact-driven business model is loved by CXOs. These are individuals who possess skills so rare, even their short stint can feel like 10x the work accomplished.

Can't this be achieved with an internal team?

the internal team is often capable, but they are already burdened with upcoming sprint, feature promised during sales call, P0 issues, recruitment, managerial bureaucracy etc.

Mercenary programmers skip all of that, are answerable to no one, are brutal in their assessments, do not sugarcoat responses and are allowed to choose the best (paid) tool for a given job. When you uncage a bird, it can do incredible things.

Why is it the end of mercenary programmers?

I've been professionally programming for 15 years. I've worn the mercenary programmer hat before and have worked with many great programmers too. But with AI making knowledge commoditised, those once-rare skills are now just a prompt away.

- migrating a large application from one programming language to another.
- fix the application becoming slow when there are a lot of users.
- identify and fix a nasty memory leak in the app.
- upgrade the app has not been updated in 15 years to the latest framework version.
- check the app for HIPAA compliance.
- implement redundancy / reduce latency / improve performance / reduce server cost
- increase the throughput of a service to 50k RPS

Having experienced the capabilities of frontier models and work dry up even before the arrival of AGI, it's unimaginable what a post-AGI world will look like, how would the jobs of the future be?

Now that everyone has wings, I would love to see extraordinary, unfathomable things get built.

items.title: Era of AI Programmers
items.summary: I've been occasionally trying AI at work on and off for a while. So here is my assessment as someone who's been into programming for…
items.content_html:
I've been occasionally trying AI at work on and off for a while. So here is my assessment as someone who's been into programming for more than a 15 years and have learnt programming the hard way (books, blogs, documentation, reading source code).
  1. AI bankrupts your thinking ability.
  2. AI has got really good at entry level noob tasks.
    • Want to create 1,500 words content? easy.
    • Want to create engaging landing pages? easy.
    • Want to create CRUD app? easy.
  3. AI struggles at really hard problems. You'd never be able to code enterprise grade product with AI (just yet).
    • At work, I could write algorithms to generate trading signals. Impossible to do it with AI.
    • Write performant code taking into consideration current vs future scale. 
    • Sometimes the smallest code change can have the biggest impact. AI can never develop the human intelligence to make that small change.
  4. While AI can never be in the arena, AI programmers would struggle to sense what's wrong with their app without thinking from first principles.
  5. Sometimes AI tries to cheat (a.k.a hallucinations), so developers who just click "Accept" are introducing bugs into software every day.
  6. Everyone's got their unique coding style and that introduce a personality into the codebase. AI spits out code with zero personality, often robotic.
  7. AI defenders claiming that there would be more jobs, are dismissing the fact that there will be more noise than signal. For end users it's going to be extremely hard to differentiate between signals and subconsciously their mind would fall back on big-tech while making software purchase decisions.
  8. Industrial scale manufacturing created the problem of plenty, often leading to landfills. In this AI era, we are already seeing exponential growth in creation of vibe coded projects often getting flipped/shut down leading to long term decline in trust. 
    • eg: Product hunt is now mostly AI apps submissions and the platform is now  already dead.
  9. Finally, there aren't those many jobs to feed 8 billion people. Not everything needs to be made at industrial scale.

items.title: Ease of maintenance is a feature
items.summary: As a person in tech, I see that there is a lot of emphasis on scalability, speed, the next shiny doll that everyone wants to…
items.content_html:
As a person in tech, I see that there is a lot of emphasis on scalability, speed, the next shiny doll that everyone wants to implement in their code, put it on their resume. But little emphasis is given on ease of maintenance. 

I say ease of maintenance is a feature.

Ease of maintenance is how long it takes for someone to

  1. Clone the source code
  2. Set up the codebase while also installing all the relevant dependencies
  3. Boot the codebase on a local machine
  4. Make that one-line change
  5. Do a small smoke test to ascertain everything is working correctly
  6. Push the changes to git or other versioning system
  7. Watch the CI/CD pipeline run and see the changes live
    • In some cases, this may also mean manually triggering a deploy because CD is not automated.

If it takes you more than an hour to go through all the above steps, you are not maintaining the software, you are fighting against a complex, "shiny" piece of tech that's so good it takes ages to ship even a small one-line change.

Software should be built to future-proof against the following scenarios:

  • Software ownership changes
  • Developers move on
  • That "shiny" piece of tech may not be maintained a year from now
  • There is a financial crisis, and the original code author is not available anymore
  • The team is too busy with other growth areas, but high maintenance is high friction.
  • The team is downsized from 100 engineers to 10 engineers, and not everyone would have experience with the codebase.
  • Certain skills are so rare it's impossible/beyond budget to hire talent for those skills.

Software should be built to last forever.

items.title: The Greater Good
items.summary: When you perform actions that might not benefit you in any way and can sometimes not be in the best interest of your own-self, however,…
items.content_html:
When you perform actions that might not benefit you in any way and can sometimes not be in the best interest of your own-self, however, if the impact on the community is profound. Congratulations, you are a part of the "greater good" club. 

Try answering the following questions

  • Why is the tax collection in many countries still so low?
  • Why is corruption so rampant in the developing world?
  • Why did some countries had and continue to have dictators?
  • Why is healthcare so unaffordable?
  • Why do politicians sometimes find ways to stay in power forever?
  • Why are some discoveries important to human existence patented?
  • Why does society have so much wealth inequality?
  • Why did the slave trade exist?
  • Why do politicians in some countries amass a fortune in their lifetime?

The answer to many of the questions above can be attributed to self-first philosophy, partly attributed to "scarcity" era which has conditioned humans to keep accumulating in fear of uncertainty. Therefore, because of this ingrained human trait, we have more humans who keep their self-interest first, instead of thinking of their community, locality, city, state, country and planet.

Statistically, if human kindness is Gaussian distributed, we should still have about 2% of the world population above Mean + 2SD (standard deviation). Lets call them humans with extreme compassion. 2% of 8 billion humans is still 160 million people, but we aren't reading about examples of extreme human compassion that often. What if the mean itself is heavily tilted towards self-interest philosophy, this could probably be due to human evolution wherein genetically we are programmed to survive first. Survival of the fittest is the game we are playing still now.

But there exist individuals who have made significant contributions to humanity, whilst not enriching oneself[1]. Imagine a world where we have more people in the "greater good" club when compared to the "self-first" group. Wouldn't the world be such a lovely place to live?

Examples:
- How one company gave up a patent—and saved 1 million lives
